title: Edge Cost Compass — scratchpad for console guidance UX
body:
Context / problem statement:

We give customers a lot of knobs (batching, quantization, model variant, routing policy, cache TTL) but most teams don’t know which knobs move cost vs latency vs quality for their workload. Console shows raw metrics today; need a lightweight guidance surface that: (a) interprets observed traffic/SLAs, (b) points to low-effort high-impact changes, and (c) lets devs simulate trade-offs before making changes.

Working name: Edge Cost Compass (ECC) — a small interactive panel in the Console route/model view that gives one-line recommendations, a heuristic explanation, and a what-if slider to preview cost/latency/quality impact.

High-level goals:
- Reduce time-to-first-cost-win for teams (from exploration to change)
- Surface low-regret defaults customers can apply in 1 click (e.g., enable KV prefix cache, switch to 8-bit variant, cap max_tokens)
- Provide transparent rationale so engs trust suggestions (show sample requests and why suggestion helps)

Primary audience: engineers and infra/platform folks using Redwood Console to monitor routes and models. Secondary: Solutions engineers helping customers optimize.

Core experience sketches (text):
1) Compact panel on route detail page: "Edge Cost Compass" with a colored needle (green/yellow/red) reflecting current cost-efficiency relative to peers/past baseline.
2) Top single recommendation (one line) + confidence: e.g. "Enable KV prefix caching — likely 18–30% token cost reduction for this route (high confidence)"
3) Expand to see: short why, sample impacted requests, estimated impact on latency and quality, and 3 quick actions: "Preview what-if" slider, "Apply change" (1-click config patch), "Open deeper analysis".
4) What-if slider: move along cost <-> latency or cost <-> quality axis. Slider calculates new estimated monthly spend and 90th p99 latency band and shows a synthetic example reply to indicate quality delta.

Heuristic rules (starter):
- If >70% of tokens are repeated prefixes across requests => recommend KV prefix caching.
- If average sequence length < 128 and model variant is large => recommend smaller model/8-bit quantization suggestion.
- If bursty traffic causing small batches (mean batch size < 2) => suggest request multiplexing or configure a slight batching hold (with latency SLO guard).
- If many requests hit same embeddings/model for reranking => suggest LRU cache for embeddings with TTL.

User stories (rough):
- As an engineer, I want one concise optimization I can apply safely so that I reduce spend without spending days instrumenting.
- As an SRE, I want to preview the latency impact of increasing batching hold so I can balance P99 requirements.
- As a solutions engineer, I want to export a list of recommendations across a customer’s top-10 routes to propose a quarterly cost-ops plan.

Acceptance / success criteria (MVP):
- Panel appears on route detail and model detail pages for customers with >= 3k tokens/day on the route.
- At least 4 heuristic checks implemented and validated on historical tracing data.
- Preview simulation accuracy within +/- 20% of actual measured change when applied on a small canary traffic slice (test across 3 customers).
- 1-click apply path executes a safe rollout (canary 5% -> 25% -> 100% with rollback).

Metrics to measure (post-launch):
- Fraction of routes with at least one recommendation acted upon within 30 days (target 10% initially).
- Median cost reduction on routes that applied suggestions within 60 days (target 12% per route).
- False positive rate (recommendation then reverted) < 10%.
- Time to first action (console session -> apply change) median < 8 minutes.

Prototype data model (simple):
- Observables: avg tokens per request, token distribution (prefix repeat rate), batch size distribution, pct of requests hitting same model/version, p50/p95/p99 latency, error rate, quality regressions (if eval sets available).
- Heuristic output: [{recommendation_id, label, confidence, estimated_cost_delta_pct, estimated_latency_delta_ms, short_reason}]

Quick sketch of API endpoints (proto):
- GET /routes/:id/edge-cost-compass -> returns heuristics + metadata + sample payloads
- POST /routes/:id/edge-cost-compass/preview -> body: {recommendation_id, simulation_axis, intensity} -> returns simulated metrics
- POST /routes/:id/edge-cost-compass/apply -> body: {recommendation_id, rollout_config} -> triggers config change and returns rollout job id

Experiments plan (alpha -> beta):
- Alpha: internal only, run on synthetic workloads and one internal customer (Mika’s test org). Validate heuristics and preview accuracy.
- Beta: enable for small set of willing customers, expose 1-click apply but limit to non-invasive changes (cache TTL, batching params). Monitor revert/rollback signals.

Open questions / risks:
- Quality measurement: how do we surface quality degradation? We can show diff on synthetic sample but that’s noisy. Need per-route eval harness (tie to existing micro-evals).
- Trust: customers may be suspicious of 1-click changes. Mitigation: clearly show canary rollout and easy rollback, and require owner confirmation.
- Multi-tenant variance: heuristics tuned on internal data may not generalize; must calibrate per-customer baseline.
- Regulatory concerns: for private deployments, ensure recommendations don’t expose telemetry outside the customer boundary.

Dependencies:
- Trace/telemetry team: expose token-level distributions and sample payloads (anonymized) to ECC service.
- Serving runtime: support dynamic toggles for KV cache and live updateable batching policies.
- Console UI: component for slider + synthetic response preview.

Next steps (immediate):
1) Quick spike: implement 2 heuristics (prefix cache detection, small-sequence model downsize) against last 30 days of traffic in internal orgs. Owner: Harish. (2 week spike)
2) Wire basic preview API and small React panel prototype. Owner: Console FE (REQ: one-day pair with infra).
3) Sync with Runtime team on what can be toggled with zero-deploy versus requires model restart. Owner: Mika.
4) Write go/no-go alpha checklist (safety, preview accuracy thresholds).

Notes to self / todo brain-dump:
- Consider a "why this matters" microcopy: show monthly $ delta + how many developer-hours saved if automated.
- Add audit log entry for any 1-click change with link to rollback and to the exact model/version changed.
- Think about a "compass history" to track prior recommendations and outcomes for route-specific learning.
- If we can get a reliable quality classifier (binary accept/reject) that would help reduce risk on model-downgrade recommendations.

Links / references:
- Related playbook: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Cost+Playbook
- Prior experiment: PROJ-724 (batching hold experiments)
- Console PR with similar UX: https://github.com/redwood-inference/console/pull/391

Bottom line: goal is to turn the Console from a passive metrics surface into a small, trustable advisor that nudges teams toward low-friction cost wins. Keep scope tiny for MVP: focus on cache + model-size heuristics + safe canary apply.
